title: Harcourt Trophies Grade 2 Teacher Guide — Day 1 Detail Pages (Phonics, Spelling, Writer's Craft, Grammar)
callouts: different supplements based on level - below, on level and advanced
writers craft has writing everyday section to the left that shows what will be explored by day

leveledSupplements.description: At the bottom of the phonics page, four leveled worksheet thumbnails appear side by side: Below-Level ('Extra Support, p. 1'), On-Level ('Practice Book, p. 1' + 'Homework Option'), Advanced ('Challenge, p. 1'), and English-Language Learners ('ELL, p. 1'). Each targets the SAME phonics skill (-id, -ide) but at a different complexity level. The parent/teacher picks the appropriate worksheet for their child's level.
leveledSupplements.pattern: Same skill, different scaffolding. Below-Level has more support/cloze; On-Level is the standard practice; Advanced adds rhymes/riddles/creative extension; ELL focuses on visual/contextual support.
leveledSupplements.value: Built-in differentiation without creating separate curricula. One week plan, four difficulty levels of worksheets.

fiveDayProgressionBadge.description: Both Spelling and Grammar pages have a color-coded 5-day progression badge in the top-left corner. Spelling: Day 1 Pretest/Word Sort → Day 2 Word Building → Day 3 State the Generalization → Day 4 Review → Day 5 Posttest/Writing Application. Grammar: Day 1 Introduce Sentences → Day 2 Review/Generate → Day 3 Review → Day 4 Review → Day 5 Cumulative Review/Identify. Current day is highlighted in red.
fiveDayProgressionBadge.value: Parent always knows where they are in the weekly arc AND where they're heading. No 'are we done yet?' anxiety.

writingEveryDay.description: The Writer's Craft page has a 'Writing Every Day' sidebar on the left showing the 5-day writing progression: Day 1 Analyze Topics and Ideas → Day 2 Focus on Topics → Day 3 Focus on Ideas → Day 4 Prewrite and Draft → Day 5 Revise, Edit, and Share Sentences. Below that, 'Traits of Good Writing' lists the four quality indicators (Focus/Ideas, Organization, Word Choice, Conventions).

days.day1: Analyze Topics and Ideas — discuss a topic and idea list
days.day2: Focus on Topics — examine choosing a topic
days.day3: Focus on Ideas — use a topic to communicate an idea

writingEveryDay.value: Writing isn't a one-day exercise — it's a week-long process with a clear pipeline: analyze → focus → draft → revise. The child sees writing as iterative, not one-shot.

diagnosticCheckSidebar.description: The phonics page has a 'Reaching All Learners' sidebar with a diagnostic check: 'If... children need additional support... Then... have children read the Decodable Books.' This is an IF/THEN remediation branch — if the child struggles with the main lesson, here's exactly what to do.
diagnosticCheckSidebar.value: The parent doesn't have to figure out what to do when a child is stuck. The decision tree is built in.

teachModelApply.description: Grammar follows a Teach/Model → Practice/Apply structure. Teach introduces the concept ('What makes a sentence?'). Practice/Apply uses a transparency with real examples. The pattern is consistent across all skill pages.
teachModelApply.value: Every lesson has the same rhythm: concept → model → practice. Predictable for both parent and child.

skillTrace.description: The Grammar page has a 'Skill Trace' box showing page references for Introduce, Reteach, Review (across multiple pages), and Test. This is a cross-reference map showing EVERYWHERE this grammar skill appears in the system.
skillTrace.value: Parent can find related practice pages instantly. No hunting through the book.

wrapUpReadAloud.description: The Grammar page ends with a 'Wrap Up: Read a Story Aloud' section — read 'The Thing That Bothered Farmer Brown,' assign animal sounds to groups, and have children imitate sounds during re-reading. Ends with SSR (Self-Selected Reading). The day doesn't end on grammar drill — it ends on joy.
wrapUpReadAloud.value: Day closure is story-based and playful, not more worksheets.

overallLayout.structure: sectioned — main content area + left sidebar (diagnostic/daily progression) + right sidebar (objectives/skill trace) + bottom row (leveled worksheets)
overallLayout.spacing: dense but well-organized — color-coded sections prevent overwhelm
overallLayout.visualHierarchy: main instruction body dominates, sidebars provide context/navigation, bottom thumbnails show differentiation options
overallLayout.flowDirection: top-down within page, sidebars provide lateral context

difficulty.complexity: multi-skill (phonics + spelling + writing + grammar, all Day 1)
difficulty.scaffolding: high — multiple scaffold levels available per skill

theming.colorPalette: full-color — day badges, section headers, diagnostic sidebars all color-coded

gaps.name: leveled-worksheet-set
gaps.description: Generate the same skill practice at multiple difficulty levels (below-level, on-level, advanced) so the parent picks the right one for their child. This is differentiation without separate curricula.

gaps.name: daily-instruction-guide
gaps.description: A parent-facing daily instruction page that includes: objective, teach/model steps, practice/apply activities, diagnostic IF/THEN branch for struggling learners, and leveled worksheet options. Not a worksheet — a teaching guide.

notes: Fourth drop from the same Trophies book. This is the 'zoom in' layer — the detailed Day 1 instruction that the lesson planner summarized in one column. Carolyng specifically called out: (1) leveled supplements (below/on/advanced), and (2) the 'Writing Every Day' sidebar showing the week's writing progression. This adds a FOURTH layer to the curriculum architecture: Lesson Planner (weekly overview) → Daily Instruction Guide (detailed teaching steps) → Practice Worksheets (student pages) → Assessments (verification). The leveled differentiation is a major new signal — she wants materials that adapt to the child's level, not one-size-fits-all.
